in addition to the graduation requirements described in Section R277-700-6, beginning with the 2016-17 school year, a student pursuing a college degree after graduation shall: (a) receive one of the following:

(i) a score of 3 or higher on an Advanced Placement (AP) calculus AB or BC exam; (ii) a score of 3 or higher on an Advanced Placement (AP) statistics exam; (iii) a score of 5 or higher on an International Baccalaureate (IB) higher level math exam;

(iv) a score of 50 or higher on a College Level Exam Program (CLEP) pre-calculus or calculus exam; (v) a score of 26 or higher on the mathematics portion of the American College Test (ACT) exam; (vi) a score of 640 or higher on the mathematics portion of the Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT) exam; or

ruleSets.title: Utah high school graduation requirements
ruleSets.plainSummary: Utah requires at least 24 credits in set subjects to graduate. The classes of 2027 and 2028 need 3 social studies credits; the class of 2029 and later need 3.5, including a new American government class. College-bound students also show they're ready for college math, or take math in 12th grade.

of.label: Grade 11 language arts
of.note: ENGL 1010 taken in 2026-27 or later counts for level 11 only through an approved ENGL 1010 pilot. Ask your counselor whether your class is part of one.

ask.question: Is my school's ENGL 1010 an approved pilot, so it counts for level 11 English?

of.label: Grade 12 language arts
of.note: Level 12 can be English 12, concurrent enrollment English, AP or IB English, or a class on the state's applied and advanced list (such as creative writing, debate or journalism).

requirements.label: Math

of.label: Secondary Math I, II and III

on.label: A third math credit from the state's applied list
on.note: Some of these are half-credit classes, so it can take two. Modern Mathematics also counts; ask your counselor how your school lists it.

of.label: 3 math credits in grades 9-12
of.note: A math class passed before 9th grade still leaves 3 math credits to earn in high school.

of.label: A calculus class with a C or better
of.note: This counts once you've passed a calculus class with a C or better. Until then, Secondary Math I, II and III is the route we plan.

requirements.note: Passing a calculus class with a C or better finishes the math requirement, however many math credits you have.

of.label: Two of the five foundation science areas
U.S. Government and Citizenship
of.note: U.S. Government and Citizenship is retired in 2027-28; seniors that year take the new American Constitutional Government and Citizenship class instead.

requirements.label: Physical education
requirements.note: A full school sport season can earn half a credit toward Participation Skills or Lifetime Activities, with your district's approval.

requirements.label: General financial literacy
requirements.note: Only General Financial Literacy counts (Finance CE counted through 2026-27). Mathematics of Personal Finance doesn't count here.

requirements.label: Total credits
requirements.note: This is the state minimum. Your district may require more.

warnings.text: 24 credits is the state minimum. Your district may require more, so check your school's total with your counselor.
High school classes you pass before 9th grade count toward graduation, and their grades go into your 9th-grade GPA. They may affect scholarship or college eligibility, so check first.
Up to half a credit of language arts can come from a class or school activity focused on speaking, such as debate.
A parent can opt a student out of Secondary Math III in writing, but the state warns this leaves students unprepared for college math.
A concurrent enrollment science class counts as a foundation science only in its version with a lab.
A 2026 law lets each district decide whether applied crafts and technical arts classes, such as woodworking, count for arts credit. Ask your counselor what your district allows.

testRoutes.text: College-bound students show they're ready for college math with one of these: an AP Calculus or AP Statistics score of 3 or higher, an IB higher level math score of 5 or higher, a CLEP precalculus or calculus score of 50 or higher, an ACT math score of 26 or higher, an SAT math score of 640 or higher, or a C in a concurrent enrollment math class that meets the college quantitative literacy requirement. Otherwise, take a full year of math in 12th grade.
